summary: Monolith Django on DigitalOcean App Platform with DigitalOcean Managed PostgreSQL as the database; front end: Django templates + HTMX.

frontend.justification: Server-rendered pages from the same Django codebase, no separate SPA. Fit for this project: team.languages includes Python; strong cost for Django templates + HTMX (priority 5); strong time to market for Django templates + HTMX (priority 5); well suited to internal tool projects.

alternatives.why_not: Scored 7.9 points lower: the team would have to learn JavaScript/TypeScript; the chosen option wins on team.languages (team.languages includes Python).
Scored 9.8 points lower: the team would have to learn JavaScript/TypeScript; the chosen option wins on team.languages (team.languages includes Python).

tradeoffs: Highly interactive UIs (drag/drop, live canvases) get awkward.

backend.justification: Ships auth, admin panel, ORM and migrations out of the box. Fit for this project: team.languages includes Python; strong time to market for Django (priority 5); well suited to internal tool projects; built-in admin/back-office screens.

alternatives.why_not: Scored 11.2 points lower: the chosen option wins on project.type (well suited to internal tool projects).
Scored 14.1 points lower: operational burden (ops 2/5) with no DevOps engineer; learning curve 3/5 for a beginner team; the chosen option wins on project.type (well suited to internal tool projects).

tradeoffs: Heavier per-request overhead than Go/Node for very high RPS.

database.justification: ACID transactions, JSONB, full-text search, PostGIS and pgvector in one engine. Fit for this project: strong cost for PostgreSQL (priority 5); strong maintainability for PostgreSQL (priority 3); strong security for PostgreSQL (priority 3); strong time to market for PostgreSQL (priority 5).

alternatives.why_not: Scored 1.3 points lower: the chosen option wins on project.type (well suited to internal tool projects).
Scored 1.2 points lower: the chosen option wins on priorities.cost (strong cost for PostgreSQL (priority 5)).

tradeoffs: Horizontal write scaling needs partitioning, read replicas or Citus.

hosting.justification: Simple PaaS with a Bengaluru (BLR1) region and managed Postgres. Fit for this project: strong time to market for DigitalOcean App Platform (priority 5); strong cost for DigitalOcean App Platform (priority 5); strong performance for DigitalOcean App Platform (priority 3).

alternatives.why_not: Scored 14.1 points lower: close runner-up; the chosen option combines better with the rest of the stack.
Scored 15.8 points lower: static hosting only; the API must run elsewhere.

tradeoffs: Fewer managed services than AWS/GCP/Azure (no managed search or ML).
Core stack starts near $12/month against a $10 budget.

supporting.justification: Uses the backend framework's maintained auth library, so user data stays in your own database.
tradeoffs: Account recovery and MFA flows must still be designed.

supporting.justification: Runs tests and deploys on every merge; free minutes cover a small team.
Free Developer plan catches crashes in the app and mobile clients with stack traces.

alternatives.why_not: Strong product but expensive per host at this budget.

assumptions: Scale level L1: ~60 users, ~10 peak concurrent, ~2 req/s at peak, ~0.1 GB stored
List prices for the smallest production tier that fits; no reserved-instance or startup credits; excludes domains, app-store fees, SMS and payment-gateway transaction fees
